title: Install, recover, or migrate Todo
summary: Initialize or migrate Todo's database, or deploy, validate, diagnose, and recover the user-owned macOS installation and daily email service.
use_when: Todo storage must be initialized or upgraded through its supported backup-bearing migrator.
The installed CLI, content-addressed release, configuration, database, or daily email LaunchAgent must be deployed or diagnosed.
do_not_use_when: The task is normal Todo domain use.
A database backup destination already exists or is relative for a required version-one migration.
The user has not authorized an installed-state or service change.
outcome: A validated current Todo database and user-owned installation with explicit backup, rollback, configuration, Nucleus, email, and service state.
effects: Initialization creates a new empty database and refuses to replace an existing path.
Migration creates a retained complete backup before the version-two transaction; current databases are true no-ops.
Deployment stages and switches content-addressed releases, may migrate the database, rewrites installed configuration when requested, and installs or updates the daily email LaunchAgent.
Deployment rollback can restore captured database, release, configuration, plist, and loaded-service state before commit.
authority: Todo owns its SQLite schema, migration, installation, configuration, and email LaunchAgent.
Nucleus remains separately authoritative for research execution and authentication; Resend remains authoritative for email submission.
success: The selected database is current and inspectable, and any required pre-migration backup remains at the explicit caller-owned path.
The installed CLI smoke test, Nucleus readiness, email preview/send validation, and LaunchAgent status are checked as applicable.
A failed pre-commit update restores the exact captured installed state.
failure_and_recovery: Ordinary commands never migrate implicitly; stop callers and use the supported migrator.
On interrupted deployment, inspect the deployer's rollback result, selected release, database, configuration, plist, and loaded service before retrying.
Do not infer 09:00 delivery while the Mac is off or the user is logged out; a user LaunchAgent cannot guarantee it.
privacy: The Todo database, migration backups, configuration, and logs can expose directions, notes, paths, design state, and email metadata.
`RESEND_API_KEY` remains in the process environment and `~/.zshrc`; Nucleus credentials remain outside Todo.
does_not_authorize: Deleting retained Todo database, backups, logs, or releases.
Changing the Resend account or exposing its API key.

consumers.statement: A current-user operator with explicit installed-state authority may initialize or migrate one Todo database or deploy, diagnose, validate, or recover Todo's macOS installation and daily email service.
Ordinary Todo domain use, release publication, retained-state deletion, and incidental external email sending are outside this capability.

preconditions.statement: Initialization targets an absent database path; a version-one migration targets a stopped database and an absent absolute caller-owned backup path.
Deployment requires an absolute tested Todo binary, healthy compatible Nucleus, explicit installed-state authority, and complete sender and recipient configuration on first install.

inputs.statement: Supported inputs are exact database, backup, binary, sender, recipient, installation, and documented wait or environment selectors for the chosen operation.
Relative or existing required migration backups, partial email configuration, foreign provider selectors, stored Resend credentials, and implicit migration are rejected.

outputs.statement: Database operation returns a new current database, a current migrated database plus retained complete backup, or a true no-op for an already-current database.

Deployment returns a validated content-addressed current release, stable command and Todo-owned provider selectors, current database and config, and installed daily email LaunchAgent, with previous release retained when applicable.

data_semantics.statement: Migration preserves historical Todo identities and records conservatively and does not infer cross-todo relationships, assessments, accepted design, implementation, or closure evidence.
The release identity covers the binary, deployer, and complete Chancery bundle; the selected config owns database and email addresses while RESEND_API_KEY remains environment-only.

identity_and_units.statement: SQLite schema version, Todo package and provider release, content-addressed release hash, LaunchAgent label org.todo.daily-email, and public Todo IDs are separate identities.
The daily occurrence is 09:00 in the Mac's current local clock; migration backup paths and release selectors identify exact filesystem objects.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A required migration writes a complete pre-transaction SQLite backup, and deployment stages and manifests every packaged binary, deployment, and provider-document byte before switching selectors.
Post-switch validation checks installed version and help, database and configuration shape, Nucleus readiness, and email service state as applicable to the deployment.
Installation success does not prove future Nucleus availability, final email receipt, or exact 09:00 execution while the user session or Mac is unavailable.

access.statement: Operations run as the current user and own only Todo's selected database, config, release, command, provider selector, LaunchAgent, and logs.
The deployer does not take over foreign selectors, store credentials, modify Nucleus authentication or state, or delete caller-retained backups and releases.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Ordinary Todo commands never migrate; explicit migration backs up before one transaction, and current databases are no-ops that leave the supplied backup path untouched.

Deployment stages content-addressed bytes, quiesces the email service, backs up and migrates, switches and validates selectors, then installs the service; any pre-commit failure restores captured database and installed state.

operational_limits.statement: Todo owns no daemon; the only service is one user LaunchAgent invoking the synchronous email command, and deployment changes only Todo-owned installation paths.
No database-size, migration-duration, deployment-duration, email-delivery, retained-release-count, or uptime service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 1 supports explicit backup-bearing migration to SQLite schema 2 and content-addressed release rollback with package and provider releases kept equal.
An update may preserve an existing complete email config byte-for-byte or replace it only when both sender and recipient are supplied together.
No perpetual support window for older database, macOS, launchd, Nucleus, Resend, or provider-schema versions is promised.

reliances.statement: Deployment readiness relies on the installed Nucleus operation contract for the execution service state required by Todo research.
Email validation and later scheduled submission rely on Resend, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes that external service promise.
Installation and scheduled daily digest execution rely on per-user launchd supervision, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes launchd readiness.
